hypothesis: The CLI raw JSON boundary currently uses a permissive decoder and path read. Contradictory duplicate keys can silently choose a source revision, and a FIFO can block before packet validation. A strict bounded regular-file reader and unambiguous JSON decoder should refuse these inputs while preserving all canonical decision cases.
scope: Local experimental lifecycle CLI admission; no production Ruby route, server, dataset promotion or model change.
controls: Conflicting duplicate current_source capable of masking a still-present function
FIFO, directory, leaf symlink and oversized input
No candidate output when raw admission refuses
policy: Reject duplicate keys instead of silently choosing first or last.
Decode strict UTF-8 and reject nonfinite JSON or unpaired surrogate strings.
Read only a bounded stable regular file with no-follow and nonblocking admission on supported platforms.
Canonical typed-dictionary decision semantics remain unchanged.
Preserve old source, raw adversarial input, timeout evidence and before/after outputs.
parallel_audit: Audit the52retained model responses for the same lexical ambiguity and every schema keyword actually used, without new inference.
limits: Strict raw admission is not semantic proof, authenticated source authority or a generic filesystem sandbox.
Current API dictionary callers have already decoded their inputs and must enforce their own raw boundary.
No ambiguous raw fixture becomes approved training data.
